text:
OpenAI released GPT-5 on August 7, 2025 [Source: ev-1], marking a deliberate strategic shift to adopt "give-away-the-frontier" pricing by making the model available immediately to free users [Source: ev-1]. This launch fundamentally changed how OpenAI sells its models in three key ways:

**Unified Model Offering**
The release ended the previous split between reasoning and non-reasoning products [Source: ev-1]. Separate o-series products—specifically o3, o4-mini, o3-mini, and o3-pro—were retired and folded into GPT-5's internal "reasoning modes," eliminating the need for a separate model picker [Source: ev-1]. As part of this consolidation, OpenAI positioned GPT-5 as a single unified model that thinks rather than just a specific type of reasoning model [Source: ev-1]. The new system includes features such as a 5-million-token context window, native image generation without requiring a separate image model, integrated deep research, and built-in file upload and web search capabilities [Source: ev-1].

**Pricing Structure**
The launch resulted in collapsed prices compared to previous offerings [Source: ev-1]. For subscriptions, users can access GPT-5 for free on the base tier; Plus subscribers pay $20/month for unlimited usage of GPT-5; and Pro access costs $200/month [Source: ev-1]. API pricing is set at $1.25 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens for GPT-5, while GPT-5 mini costs $0.25 per million input tokens and 2 dollars per million output tokens [Source: ev-1].

**Competitive Focus**
The competitive battleground shifted from benchmark demos to "default agency," focusing on models that act rather than just answer questions [Source: ev-1]. In terms of performance relative to this new value proposition, GPT-5 scored approximately 78.6% on SWE-bench Verified, with GPT-5 mini scoring closely behind at these reduced price points [Source: ev-1].
